Development where the investment case governs the specification. Underwriting-first delivery for private investors, family offices and specialist funds. Focus: refurb-and-refinance, HMO conversion, small-site residential, and Private Rented Sector feasibility.

Underwriting

IRR, MOIC, capex, funding cost and exit case modelled before an offer is made, not after.

Acquisition support

Why the investment case has to govern the spec

The classic mistake on a small residential development is a specification set against an aesthetic wishlist and reconciled to the numbers at Stage 4, when it is too late. The result is a scheme that cannot refinance at the assumed values, or that sells below GDV because the unit mix is wrong, or that runs out of contingency at second fix. Value engineering after that point trades a strategic error for a tactical one.

Investment-led development inverts the sequence. The IRR, LTV, refinance case and exit are agreed first, and the specification, unit mix and programme are drawn to hit them. Design and value engineering are then two views of the same conversation, not a fight held at two different meetings six months apart.

How we deliver, in order

  1. Acquisition supportDesktop planning check, sketch cost plan and sketch GDV inside the offer window; go/no-go before exchange.
  2. UnderwritingIRR, MOIC, refi and exit sensitivity, funding cost and drawdown schedule modelled against realistic contingency.
  3. Design to spec that hits GDVConcept design, unit mix, spec and finishes drawn against the comparables and the target buyer or tenant.
  4. Planning risk assessmentPre-application if warranted; Article 4, listed status, HMO licensing route or permitted-development route documented before design fees run.
  5. TenderTwo-stage tender to selected subcontractors, or negotiated route with our supply chain; priced against a coordinated design.
  6. DeliveryEnabling works through superstructure to fit-out, with monthly QS report to the funder's monitoring surveyor.
  7. PC & warrantyStatutory sign-offs, structural warranty issued, refi-ready pack assembled.
  8. Refi or exitRefinance drawdown or sale-ready marketing pack; option to roll onto a lettings and PPM contract for long-hold assets.

Frequently asked questions

Do you take equity or work as a contractor?

Both, in separate agreements. On some schemes we deliver strictly under a JCT contract for a fixed or target cost. On others we co-invest with the sponsor, taking an equity stake in a special-purpose vehicle. The two roles are documented separately so the risks are not commingled and any conflict is transparent to any other equity partner or lender.

How does an Article 4 direction affect HMO viability?

Article 4 directions in many London boroughs (Barking and Dagenham, Barnet, Camden, Newham, Redbridge, Waltham Forest and others) remove permitted development from Use Class C3 (dwellinghouse) to C4 (small HMO). Where Article 4 is in force, planning permission is required for the change of use, and the viability of the scheme has to account for planning risk, application fees, professional costs and the programme impact.

How is the specification set?

The specification is set against the exit case: comparable sales values at that postcode for the target unit type, or comparable rents and yield for a PRS or HMO exit. The finishes, MEP, kitchen and bathroom spec, and any smart-home or amenity provision, are calibrated to hit the value bracket without over-specifying and eroding IRR.

What cash-out timelines are realistic?

A small refurbishment can refinance within 8 to 14 months from purchase to drawdown, depending on planning position and works scope. A ground-up small-site development typically runs 18 to 30 months. HMO conversion into a licensable HMO with planning is typically 10 to 16 months. Each is modelled up front rather than assumed.

What warranties will a purchaser expect on exit?

For a sold unit: a structural warranty (NHBC, LABC, BuildZone, ICW or CRL as appropriate), collateral warranties from the design and build team, and manufacturer warranties on the envelope, roof, kitchen and bathroom fittings. For a refi hold: the funder's monitoring surveyor's sign-off, EPC, gas safety certificate and Electrical Installation Condition Report.

Are you FCA regulated?

No. We are a contractor and, where we co-invest, a joint-venture equity partner. We do not offer investment advice, we do not pool retail investor money, and we do not operate a collective investment scheme. Investors are always sophisticated or professional counterparties acting on their own advice.
